newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares rally, electricals lead the way.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares rally, electricals lead the way.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed nearly three points higher, powering forward on strong foreign buying and expectations that a state anti-monopoly ruling will benefit Enersis and its subsidiaries, brokers said.

The blue-chip IPSA index got a slow start in early trade but surged ahead in afternoon trading, ending 2.01 percent higher to 134.78 points. The all-share IGPA ended 1.14 percent higher at 5770.01 points.
"It seems there is a lot of money coming in from abroad -- not just into Chile but the whole region," said Eleonor Lefebure, analyst at Santander Investment.
"There have been a lot of upgrades for Chile (by brokerages) and they are buying the most liquid stocks," she said, citing Enersis, Endesa and Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile.

A few fundamentals were also helping the power sector. Heavy rain in Santiago contributed to ending lingering concern about the effects of drought on power generation, and investors were convinced that a state anti-monopoly commission would rule essentially in Enersis' favor in a key lawsuit.

The anti-monopoly commission was due to rule late Wednesday on whether Enersis will be able to continue with its "vertical integration" in energy generation, transmission and distribution, brokers said.

A favorable ruling was likely to help prices for Enersis, its generation unit Endesa and distribution unit Chilectra, brokers said. The group's transmission company, Transelec, is 100 percent owned by Endesa.

A state anti-monopoly prosecutor has charged that Enersis' involvement in every stage of electricity, from generation to distribution, has had a chilling effect on the development of competition in the national power industry.
With the ruling still secret, but the market betting it will go Enersis' way, its share price rose 3.4 percent to 301 pesos. Chilectra was one of the day's top gainers, up four percent to 3120 pesos.
Heady gains in various sectors showed the market moved not just on the end of drought but on heavy foreign buying, said Lefebure. "CTC went a lot, so it's not just the rain," she said.
"Chile is being seen as expensive but safe," said a broker.

CTC rose 3.8 percent to 3710 pesos on its expected merger with long distance competitor VTR, brokers said. Santander issued a report saying it thought the market had factored in CTC's deal with VTR following sharp increases in recent weeks.

Stocks in the wine sector, where exports have been booming recently, were among the biggest gainers. Concha y Toro was up four percent to 281 pesos, and winery Undurraga was the day's top gainer, ending eight percent higher to 510 pesos.
The agriculture ministry reported first quarter wine exports rose 65 percent over the same period last year.
